# Rules for index-page

## index

### IDX-001 — One list toolbar above the table

**Rule:** Put search, filters and the view selector together in a single toolbar directly above the table.

- Why: Users scan one predictable strip to narrow a list; scattering search, filters and views around the page makes them hunt for the controls that change what the table shows.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Any list or table page with more than one screen of records or more than one way to narrow it.
- Exceptions: A short fixed list (under about 10 rows, no filtering need) can skip the toolbar entirely.
- Do: Toolbar row: view selector, search field, "Filters" button, column picker; table immediately below.
- Don't: Search in the page header, filters in a side panel and the view switcher below the table.
- Check (static): On each index page the search input, filter trigger and view selector share one container that is the previous sibling (or first child of the same section) of the table element.
- Check (live): At 1440 px, open each list page; the search, filter and view controls sit in one horizontal row between the page header and the first table row, with no other content between them and the table.

### IDX-002 — Search placeholder names the searchable fields

**Rule:** Label the list search field with the fields it actually matches, such as "Search by name or code", instead of a bare "Search".

- Why: Users cannot guess whether a list search matches IDs, names, emails or tags; naming the fields prevents empty results that look like missing data.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The list search matches a limited set of fields, or matches by prefix rather than substring.
- Exceptions: A combined search-and-filter field that parses free text and filter tokens may use a generic label if it shows the matched fields as suggestions while typing.
- Do: "Search by email" on a members list; "Search by name prefix" when only prefix matching is supported.
- Don't: A field labelled "Search" that silently matches only the record ID.
- Check (static): Every list search input has a placeholder or accessible name that names at least one field ("by ..."), and the named fields match the fields the backend query uses.
- Check (live): Type a value that appears only in a field not named in the placeholder; the list must return no match, confirming the label is accurate. Type a value from a named field; it must match.

### IDX-003 — Saved views in a selector

**Rule:** Offer a view selector in the list toolbar with preset views, and let users save the current filters, sort and columns as a named view.

- Why: People return to the same slices of a list every day; a named view turns a multi-step filter into one click and keeps the default list uncluttered.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl absent, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Lists that users filter the same way repeatedly (queues, operational lists, logs).
- Exceptions: Small reference lists with no filters do not need views. Saving user views is confirmed live in only two portals; whether views are personal or shared across the team is not established.
- Do: View menu: All, Unfulfilled, Unpaid, Archived, then user views; "Save" and "Reset view" become enabled only after the user changes a filter, sort or column.
- Don't: A "Save view" button that is always enabled, or views that store only the search text and drop sort and columns.
- Check (static): The list toolbar has a view selector (menu, combobox or button) listing at least the "All" preset; Save/Reset view controls carry disabled state bound to "current view equals saved view".
- Check (live): Change a filter; Save and Reset view enable. Save as a named view, reload, select it from the selector; the same filter, sort and columns return. Press Reset view; the unmodified view returns and the buttons disable again.

### IDX-004 — Lifecycle states as one-click segments with counts

**Rule:** When records move through a fixed lifecycle, expose each state as a one-click segment (tab or preset view) and show the count of records in states that need action.

- Why: In operational lists the main question is "what is waiting for me"; a count per state answers it before the user opens the list.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Records have a small fixed set of workflow states (about 3-7) and users act on them in order (orders, tickets, shipments, approvals).
- Exceptions: For resources with only health or status attributes and no workflow (servers, domains, tokens), a status filter or column is enough. Toolbar actions may change per state, for example a "Manifest all" action only in the Printed state.
- Do: Tabs "New 12 | Printed | Shipped | Returned | Archived"; counts load per tab with a placeholder and never block the table.
- Don't: A single unfiltered list where users must build a status filter by hand every morning.
- Check (static): Each state segment is a link or tab whose URL encodes the state; count badges are rendered from a separate request and have a loading placeholder.
- Check (live): Click each state segment; the URL changes and a reload keeps the same state. Throttle the network; the table renders before or independently of the counters. Check at 768 and 390 px that state segments stay reachable.

### IDX-005 — User-chosen columns with a reset

**Rule:** Show a default subset of columns and let users show or hide the rest from a column picker in the list toolbar or table header.

- Why: Different jobs need different fields; a picker keeps the default table readable while still giving power users every attribute.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: The record type has more attributes than fit legibly at desktop width (roughly more than 7-8 columns).
- Exceptions: Tables with a handful of fixed columns need no picker. A locked column and a "Reset to default" item were seen in one portal only; treat them as recommended, not required.
- Do: Column menu with one checkbox per column, the row-identifying column checked and disabled, and "Reset to default" at the bottom.
- Don't: Showing all 20+ attributes by default with horizontal scrolling.
- Check (static): The list toolbar or table header contains a column-picker control whose menu has one checkbox item (menuitemcheckbox or checkbox) per hideable column, and the default column set is defined in one place smaller than the full set.
- Check (live): Open the column picker, uncheck a column; it disappears from the table. Reload; it stays hidden. Check it again; it returns.

### IDX-006 — Sortable headers that show the current sort

**Rule:** Make sortable columns' headers buttons with an accessible name such as "Sort by date", and show the active column and direction.

- Why: Clicking a header is the expected way to reorder a list; without a visible direction indicator users cannot tell how the list is ordered.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Columns with a meaningful order (dates, amounts, names, counts, statuses).
- Exceptions: Columns with no natural order (tags, flags, action buttons, images) stay plain headers.
- Do: "Order date ↓" header button with aria-sort="descending"; clicking flips the direction.
- Don't: Every header clickable, including "Tags" and "Actions", with no indicator of which one is active.
- Check (static): Sortable column headers contain a button; the active one has aria-sort set (ascending/descending) and a visible arrow; non-sortable headers have no button.
- Check (live): Click a sortable header twice; row order flips and the arrow/aria-sort flips with it. Reload; the chosen sort is kept or the URL encodes it.

### IDX-007 — Paginate with range, total and page size

**Rule:** Paginate long lists (default 20-50 rows per page) and show the visible range with the total, Previous/Next controls and a rows-per-page selector.

- Why: A range with a total ("Showing 1-25 of 63") tells users how much is left and confirms a filter worked; page size lets heavy users trade scrolling for fewer clicks.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify absent, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Any list that can exceed one page of records.
- Exceptions: Append-only streams such as live logs may use load-more or infinite scroll if they keep a visible count of loaded records.
- Do: Footer: "Showing 51-100 of 412", Previous, Next, "Rows per page: 50".
- Don't: Rendering thousands of rows at once, or pagination with only page numbers and no total.
- Check (static): The list footer (or toolbar) contains Previous and Next controls with disabled states, a range-and-total text, and a page-size select; the API call carries limit/offset or a cursor.
- Check (live): On a list with more than one page, click Next; the range text updates and Previous enables. Change rows per page; the range and page count recalculate. On the last page Next is disabled.

### IDX-008 — Row selection only where bulk actions exist

**Rule:** Give a list a checkbox column with a header select-all only when it has at least one bulk action.

- Why: Checkboxes promise that something can be done to many rows at once; showing them on lists with no bulk action is noise.
- Confidence: medium (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: The list supports at least one action on several records (print, archive, delete, export selected, tag).
- Exceptions: When a bulk action only works for a compatible subset (for example the same carrier or the same status), disable it with a visible reason instead of failing after submit. The behaviour of the bulk-action bar after selection was not exercised in any portal. A select-all label that states its scope ("on page") was seen in one portal only.
- Do: "Select all 50 on page" in the header checkbox; after selecting, offer "Select all 412 matching" as an explicit second step.
- Don't: Checkbox columns on a read-only list, or a header "Select all" that silently selects every record across all pages.
- Check (static): Every list that renders a checkbox column also defines at least one bulk action in its toolbar or selection bar; every list without bulk actions renders no checkbox column.
- Check (live): On each list with checkboxes, tick one row; a bulk-action control appears or enables. Untick all; it hides or disables. Open each list without bulk actions; no row checkboxes are shown.

### IDX-009 — Row actions in a trailing overflow menu

**Rule:** Put per-row actions in the last column as an overflow menu or icon buttons, and keep primary buttons out of table rows.

- Why: A primary button on every row competes with the page's primary action and turns the table into a wall of buttons; a trailing menu keeps rows scannable and predictable.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Lists where each record has secondary actions (edit, duplicate, archive, delete, open externally).
- Exceptions: A work queue whose whole job is one repetitive action per row (for example print a label) may show that single action as a visible row button, provided it is the only button per row and the column can be hidden.
- Do: Last cell: a "..." button opening Edit, Duplicate, Archive, Delete (destructive item last, styled critical).
- Don't: Three filled buttons (Edit, Duplicate, Delete) in every row.
- Check (static): Within table rows there is no element styled as primary; row actions live in the last column inside a menu trigger or icon buttons with accessible names.
- Check (live): Open the row menu with keyboard (Tab to the trigger, Enter); the menu lists the row actions and Escape closes it, returning focus to the trigger.

### IDX-010 — Import and export as list-level actions

**Rule:** Place Import and Export as secondary actions in the header or toolbar of the list whose records they move.

- Why: Users look for import and export where they see the data; hiding them in settings or a separate area makes a routine bulk task a search.
- Confidence: high (source observed; shopify observed, dhl observed, cloudflare observed)
- Applies when: Records users need to move in bulk to or from spreadsheets, accounting or other systems.
- Exceptions: Scheduled or very large exports may also live in a reports area, provided the list links to it. Background export jobs with a status and download column were seen in one portal only, and export scope (filtered vs all) was not exercised anywhere.
- Do: Header: "Export" and "Import" left of the primary "Add"; a large export runs as a job that ends in "Export ready" with a download link.
- Don't: Export hidden only in global settings, with nothing on the list page itself.
- Check (static): Each list whose records can be imported or exported renders the Import and Export controls inside its page header or list toolbar, styled as secondary (not primary).
- Check (live): Open each list that supports import or export; Import and Export are visible without opening a menu outside the page, and clicking Export starts a download, a dialog or a job from that page.

### IDX-011 — No-match state distinct from empty list

**Rule:** When filters or search return nothing, say so and offer to clear them, instead of showing the first-use empty state.

- Why: A first-use message ("Create your first ...") on a filtered list makes users think their data is gone; a no-match message points at the filter as the cause.
- Confidence: high (source documented; shopify documented, dhl absent, cloudflare absent)
- Applies when: Any list with search or filters.
- Exceptions: None for filtered lists. The first-use empty state itself is covered by the states rules.
- Do: "No orders match these filters." with a "Clear filters" button, toolbar still visible with the active filters shown.
- Don't: An illustration saying "Create your first order" while a status filter is active on a list of 400 orders.
- Check (static): The list component renders two different empty templates, selected by whether any filter, search or non-default view is active; the no-match template contains a clear-filters action.
- Check (live): Search for a random string that matches nothing; the message mentions the filter or search and offers to clear it, and the toolbar stays visible. Clear it; the full list returns.
